Optimizing for Representation Learning

The grand success of Deep Learning is often attributed to large models' ability to learn representations of data suitable for more classical (or just simpler) machine learning methods take as input down stream. This project explores alternative algorithms that split learning representations maps (i.e. Phi) and learning task heads (i.e. F^(t)) into two seperate problems since classical methods break down or don't work well in this setting.

SwiftScore

SwiftScore is the world's first Assignment Management Platform - a SaaS tool that aims to save teachers time using AI-assisted grading, analytics, and remediation tools all in one. I worked on early engineering for the platform, particularly on integrating our services with Google Classroom. I am still involved with the company, although I am now focused on product and strategy.

Decision Making Diffusion Models

(Pre-print forthcoming) Thinking of DDPMS as a stochastic process, I explore how different time intervals in the diffusion trajectory affect the features/structure that show up in the final sample. More importantly, I learned to train large models on (multiple) GPUs, got my toes wet with generative modeling theory, and made a lot of cool friends while working on this project in Prof. Eric Wong's Brachio Lab under Anton Xue during my Sophomore summer.

TyPorch - C++ PyTorch Replica

TyPorch began as means for me to learn how ML works beyond model.fit() after my freshman Big Data course, but unintentionally became my first interaction with optimization algorithms, high performance (parallel) computing, C++, and shaped many of my interests throughout the rest of my time at Penn. I was able to train moderately sized (10k parameter) feedforward models on toy data, but never finished working all the way through benchmarking on the MNIST dataset.
